title: Hybrid quorum-based tripper and shadow-fallback playbook for per-model/dependency/tenant failures
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: implement a hybrid quorum-based circuit tripper and a safe shadow-fallback playbook that operates across per-dependency, per-model, and per-tenant dimensions. This ticket captures design, engineering tasks, test plans, and rollout strategy for a system that detects degrading dependencies via an ensemble of signals (latency quantiles, error-rate bursts, model error-rate heuristics, and region health), trips with a weighted quorum, and routes to verified fallback paths (cached prefixes, lighter model variants, regional replicas, or controlled shedding).
acceptance_criteria: A quorum tripping algorithm evaluates signals from region health, model-inference-error-rate, and tenant-specific SLA breaches and computes a trip decision within 150ms of the detecting spike

Fallback routes are registered for each model/dependency and include at least two safe options (local cached response OR lower-cost model variant OR remote replica) with documented quality/latency trade-offs
Rollout can be enabled per-tenant and per-region with feature flag and supports canary on 1% -> 10% -> 100% traffic progression with automatic rollback on regression
Monitoring and alerts surfaced: trip events with contributing signals, fallback route chosen, customer-visible latency/regression, and automated post-mortem link
Performance: additional CPU overhead on router tier <10% p50; no measurable increase in median latency for non-failing traffic
design_decisions: Use a weighted quorum: assign weights to signals (regional pod health 40%, model error-rate 30%, tenant SLO lag 20%, queue-length spikes 10%) so one noisy signal cannot force a full trip
Quorum evaluated in two phases: detect (fast local heuristic) then confirm (aggregate cross-region brief window) to avoid flapping

Fallback ranking: prefer deterministic cached prefixes (zero model compute) then quantized L2 model variant then geographically-near replica. Cache freshness TTLs and quality loss are documented for each model
Trip hysteresis uses an exponential backoff window and token-bucket based gradual increase to avoid cascade re-trips when backends recover
Provide per-tenant overrides with opt-in safe-mode (customers can request conservative trip thresholds for regulated workloads)
implementation_notes: Router-side patch: add QuorumEvaluator service that consumes existing metrics stream (prometheus push gateway + internal event bus) and exposes a 1ms decision API

State machine: CLOSED -> SOFT_TRIPPED (shadow fallback enabled) -> OPEN (strict fallback) -> RECOVERING. SOFT_TRIPPED routes a fraction of traffic to fallback and collects quality metrics before full OPEN
Signal smoothing: use quantile sketch (CKMS) for latency; short window (30s) for detection, confirm window (3x detection) for quorum confirmation
Fallback flow must be idempotent-safe; implement request fingerprinting to deduplicate when shadowing and when routing to remote replicas
Add configuration schema for fallback policies tied to model manifest (supported_fallbacks, expected_quality_delta, max_reroute_latency)
test_plan: Unit tests for QuorumEvaluator logic covering single-signal, multi-signal, and noisy-signal scenarios
End-to-end chaos test using staged failure injection: region pod failure, model worker CPU spike, and synthetic tenant spike to verify SOFT_TRIPPED behavior and eventual OPEN
Canary harness: route 1% of production traffic behind feature flag and compare embeddings/generation quality to baseline for 24h before ramp
Load tests to verify router CPU increase <10% and decision latency <150ms at 95th percentile under peak traffic
Quality gates: automatic rollback if fallback path increases user-visible failure rate by >0.5% or degrades prompt-quality scores beyond model-specific thresholds
rollout_plan: Stage 0: deploy QuorumEvaluator as opt-in behind feature flag in staging cluster and run synthetic failure scenarios
Stage 1: enable SOFT_TRIPPED for internal tenants and sample 0.5% traffic; collect fallback quality metrics for 48h
Stage 2: canary to 1% external tenants for 24h; if stable, increase to 10% over 72h
Stage 3: global enable for all tenants with per-tenant conservative knobs enabled by default for enterprise customers
Rollback: immediate feature flag off will bring system to CLOSED; automatic rollback if post-canary regressions detected by monitoring rules
monitoring: dashboards: Quorum decisions per minute, contributing signal heatmap, trip state counts by model/tenant/region
alerts: trip-rate > 5/min for single tenant OR new fallback error-rate > 0.2% sustained for 10m
SLO link: tie trip events to affected SLO windows and surface in incident queues
audit logs: every trip decision must persist contributing signal snapshot and chosen fallback route for post-incident analysis

2026-03-04 Marcus Zhang: Implemented prototype QuorumEvaluator in feature branch gh/redwood/runtime/quorum-tripper. PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/1287
2026-03-06 SRE: Reviewed confirm-window timing. Recommendation: increase confirm window to 90s for regional noise. Updated design_decisions accordingly.
2026-03-08 Product: Approved per-tenant conservative default. Note: product requests a toggle for enterprise customers to disable automatic OPEN transitions.
2026-03-09 QA: Started chaos tests with region pod drain. Observed SOFT_TRIPPED routing held quality delta at 0.18% after 2h (within gate). Continuing longer run.
notes: This ticket intentionally separates detection (fast) from confirmation (aggregate) to reduce false positives noted during last incident (INC-2026-02-model-burst).
Fallback paths must be pre-validated for each model by Model Onboarding team before being listed in config to avoid surprises at trip time.
Consider adding playback evaluation that samples the shadowed responses and scores them with the evaluation harness nightly to surface quality drift
